name: Aurelius & Strand Thermal Overcoat
description:
Aurelius & Strand is a Tier 5 tailor operating from a single atelier on the upper floors of a Spire commercial tower, accepting clients by referral only. Their Thermal Overcoat is a floor-length piece in a double-faced cashmere-wool that falls with the kind of weight that makes movement feel deliberate. The exterior is available in three colors — deep charcoal, ivory, and a midnight blue that is almost but not quite black — and the interior face, which shows at the collar and lapel turn, is a contrasting cream or dove grey. The construction is fully bespoke: the fit is calculated to the individual wearer's measurements and adjusted twice before delivery. Seams are hand-finished. The buttons are milled horn.

Embedded in the chest lining is a passive thermal regulation mesh — not advertised, not explained in any documentation, simply present — that maintains a stable microclimate around the torso across a wide range of external temperatures. The wearer stays comfortable from a heated boardroom to an outdoor arrival platform without visible adjustment. This is a jacket for people who cannot afford to be seen to be cold. In the Spire, discomfort is a form of vulnerability, and Aurelius & Strand charges accordingly for its elimination.
functionality: Passive thermal regulation mesh maintains stable torso temperature across a wide external temperature range without active power draw. No BCI interface. No visible tech.
what_it_says: You have arrived at a level where your coat costs more than most people's annual housing, and nobody in your circle will find that remarkable.
worn_by: anyone for whom the price is not a consideration
story_hooks: Two Spire board members wear Aurelius & Strand coats to the same meeting; the tailor has a strict one-client-per-sector policy, which means one of these coats is a forgery — and a very good one.

The passive thermal mesh in a specific coat is broadcasting a faint signal that its owner hasn't noticed; someone installed a secondary function during the atelier fitting, and Aurelius & Strand insists it wasn't them.

A Tier 3 investigator who spent a year building a financial fraud case against a Spire executive has managed to get inside the atelier as a cleaning contractor; the coat hanging in the workroom has a name tag that changes everything about the case.
